name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.IsPureState
title: Pure states as real extreme points

content.display_title: Pure states as real extreme points
content.one_sentence_role: Defines purity inside the normalized positive state space.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra, and let $\varphi:A\to\mathbb C$ be continuous and complex-linear. Purity is the following condition on $\varphi$.
content.definition_explanation: Write $$S(A)=\{\psi:A\to\mathbb C\text{ continuous and complex-linear}:\ \psi(a)\ge0\text{ for all }a\ge0,\ \psi(1)=1\}.$$ Then $\varphi$ is pure precisely when $\varphi\in S(A)$ and, whenever $\psi,\eta\in S(A)$ and $0<t<1$ satisfy $$\varphi=(1-t)\psi+t\eta,$$ one has $\psi=\eta=\varphi$. Equivalently, $\varphi\in\operatorname{ext}_{\mathbb R}S(A)$. Membership in the extreme-point set already includes membership in $S(A)$.
content.assumptions: The definition does not require $A\ne0$. Positivity uses the given star-compatible order on $A$ and the usual real nonnegative cone inside $\mathbb C$.
content.conclusion: A pure state is in particular a state; extremality is taken for real convex combinations.
